name: Sha Phaley
instructions: 1. Prepare the dough by mixing flour and water, kneading until smooth, then let it rest.
2. In a bowl, combine minced meat, chopped cabbage, onions, ginger, garlic, green chilies, soy sauce, salt, and pepper to make the filling.
3. Roll the dough into small circles, similar to puri or small pancakes.
4. Place a portion of the meat mixture in the center of the dough circle.
5. Fold the dough over the filling to create a semi-circle and seal the edges tightly by crimping or pressing with a fork.
6. Heat oil in a deep pan and fry the stuffed bread on medium heat until golden brown and crispy on both sides.
7. Drain excess oil and serve hot with spicy tomato chutney.
description: Sha Phaley is a popular Tibetan-origin snack widely embraced in Sikkim. It consists of bread stuffed with a seasoned meat and vegetable filling, deep-fried to perfection. It is a staple comfort food, often enjoyed as a hearty evening snack or a quick meal across the state.
